# Useful

### baseMean
The average normalised count across all six samples. It tells you how strongly the gene is expressed overall. A gene with a baseMean of 5 is barely detected; one with 50,000 is a major transcript.

### log2FoldChange
The effect size. A value of 1 means the gene is twice as high in the thin biofilm; a value of -2 means it is four times lower. Zero means no change. This is the number a biologist cares about.

### lfcSE
The standard error of the fold change estimate. Small counts give large standard errors. A large fold change with a large standard error is not evidence of anything.

### stat
The test statistic: the fold change divided by its standard error. Effect size measured in units of its own uncertainty. This is what the p-value is computed from.

### pvalue
The probability of seeing a difference this large, or larger, if the gene were truly unchanged. Not adjusted for the thousands of other genes you also tested.

### padj
That p-value adjusted for multiple testing. This is the column you filter on. Section 10 explains why.
